Background Anthracyclines are chemotherapeutic agents frequently used in breast cancer (BC) treatment. Although it improves disease-free and overall survival, the use of anthracyclines is associated with a cumulative risk of cardiac toxicity. Preventive strategies to optimize cardiac health are needed and exercise is proposed as a potential non-pharmacological approach for counteracting anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC). Most of the data on the effects of exercise to reduce ACT are from animal studies, with only a few studies in a limited number of patients indicating beneficial effects. To better understand the effectiveness of exercise in the mitigation of ARC, clinical, real-world trials claim require a larger sample size and more accurate and valuable clinical biomarkers. In this study, we intend to include a large sample and investigate cardiac function through serial measures of biomarkers and imaging techniques. Methods This protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial that will explore the cardioprotective effect of a structured exercise program in women with BC undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT). Ninety adult women with early BC and recommended to receive ACT will be randomly assigned (1:1) to an intervention group or a control group. Patients allocated to the intervention group will perform a supervised exercise program three times per week, consisting of a combination of aerobic and resistance training with progressive intensity and volume, during the time period they receive ACT. The control group will receive standard BC care. Primary outcomes related to cardiac (dys)function will be circulating N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels, resting left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain, and resting LV ejection fraction. Secondary outcomes will include the assessment of resting blood pressure, resting heart rate (HR), resting HR variability (HRV), recovery HR, physical function outcomes, self-reported physical activity level, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. Data will be obtained at baseline (t 0 ), after the end of anthracycline-treatment (t 2 ), and 3 months after t2 (t 3 ). Additionally, NT-proBNP will be measured 1–24 h prior to each anthracycline-treatment cycle (t1). Discussion The implementation of the present study design, using novel clinical biomarkers, will determine the effect of structured exercise interventions at mitigating ARC, with the overall aim of finding means to further improve BC care. Keywords Breast cancer Cardiotoxicity Cardiac healthcare Supervised exercise Supportive cancer care Banco Santander (ES) BID/ICI-FCSH/SANTANDER UNIVERSIDADES-UBI/2017 Antunes Pedro issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2019 Background Over the last three decades the epidemiology of breast cancer (BC) has been marked by the clear increase in survival rates [ 1 ]. The accessibility of screening and the discovery of new therapeutic options are among some relevant factors related to the improved management of cancer. However, despite their undeniable clinical importance, anti-cancer treatments are also associated with frequent induction of side effects. Among those, cardiotoxicity emerges as a major challenge, limiting treatment options [ 2 ] and contributing to morbidity and mortality in this patient population [ 3 – 5 ]. In the BC setting, cardiotoxicity is typically associated with exposure to traditional cytotoxic therapies and particularly with the use of anthracyclines [ 6 ]. Anthracyclines are important and effective chemotherapeutic agents, frequently administered in curative and palliative regimens for BC, although their clinical use is limited by cardiac dysfunction, usually seen as cardiotoxicity [ 7 ]. The American Society of Echocardiography and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging define cardiotoxicity as a decrease in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of > 10% to a value of < 53% [ 8 ]. However, it has been proposed that anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) is a continuous [ 9 ] and dose-dependent phenomenon [ 10 ] that starts with acute myocardial damage [ 11 ], which can be detected by elevation of circulating cardiac biomarkers [ 12 ] and by impairment of left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain [ 13 ], in turn preceding the commonly reported progressive decline in LVEF [ 9 ]. ARC may ultimately lead to overt heart failure, particularly when underestimated, not prevented or insufficiently prevented, or untreated, [ 9 ]. Unfortunately, and in addition to the manifestations associated with anthracycline treatment, BC survivors often exhibit a phenotype characterized by the presence of risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD), including advanced age, obesity, prior CVD, poor cardiorespiratory fitness, and inappropriate lifestyle (smoking, alcoholism, and sedentary lifestyle) [ 14 , 15 ]. It is therefore not surprising that when compared to healthy individuals of a similar age, these patients have higher prevalence of CVD and greater mortality [ 4 ]. Considering the high risk of cardiac dysfunction, the study of preventive strategies is an emerging and unmet need, as these strategies may mitigate cardiac damage associated with the use of cardiotoxic agents and could lead to improvements in overall cardiovascular health. In adults with CVD without cancer, exercise training is recognized as an important approach in cardiac rehabilitation [ 16 ]. Particularly, two meta-analyses have shown favorable effects of exercise on attenuation of N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) [ 17 ] and mitigation of LV remodeling [ 18 ] in patients with heart failure. Also, in the oncological setting, it has become clear that exercise is a safe and effective supportive therapy in the management of several treatment-related side effects and in improving overall physical fitness [ 19 , 20 ]. Furthermore, in a recent position paper the European Society of Cardiology task force for cancer treatments and cardiovascular toxicity suggests the possible utility of aerobic exercise as a promising strategy to attenuate ARC [ 21 ]. However, this position remains to be complementarily analyzed as the evidence so far is mainly from studies in animal models [ 22 , 23 ], with only a few studies in a limited number of patients to evaluate the cardioprotective role of exercise in cardiac function among women with breast cancer receiving cardiotoxic treatments [ 24 – 26 ]. Further clinical studies involving a large sample size and accurate clinical biomarkers are thus warranted to better understand the effectiveness of exercise in the mitigation of ARC. Hypothesis The primary aim of this study is to ascertain whether a structured exercise program mitigates ARC, measured by change in the levels of circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac (dys)function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain and LVEF). The secondary aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of the intervention in the regulation of some cardiac health parameters: resting blood pressure, resting heart rate (HR), resting HR variability (HRV) and recovery HR. As exploratory objectives, we will assess physical function (cardiorespiratory capacity, upper limb strength, and lower limb functionality), self-reported physical activity level, health-related quality of life (HR-QOL), and fatigue. We hypothesize that exercise may limit the degradation of cardiac function and structure and benefit cardiac outcomes. We also believe that patients in the intervention group will improve overall physical fitness, HR-QOL, decrease their perception of fatigue, and increase physical activity levels.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a two-arm, prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of a structured exercise program in adult women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy. The primary aim is to mitigate anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC) by assessing changes in circulating biomarkers (NT-proBNP) and cardiac function endpoints (LV global longitudinal strain, LVEF). Secondary objectives include evaluating other cardiac health parameters (blood pressure, HR, HRV, recovery HR), physical function, self-reported physical activity, health-related quality of life, and fatigue. The protocol also details the planned methodology for assessing these outcomes and administrative aspects of the study.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Structured Exercise Program (Aerobic and Resistance Training)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The intervention group will perform a supervised exercise program three times per week, during anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT). Each 70-minute session includes a 5-minute warm-up, 60 minutes of training, and a 5-minute cooldown. Aerobic training, progressively increasing from 20 to 30 minutes at light to moderate-to-high intensity (50-80% HR reserve), combines treadmill, stationary bike, and stepping. Resistance training involves 2-3 sets of 10-12 maximal repetitions (12-RM) for upper and lower body, with progressive intensity. The program starts 1-2 days after the first chemotherapy session and continues throughout treatment. The control group receives standard breast cancer care without specific physical activity advice. No dose-response comparisons are reported.

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Structured exercise program in women with early breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary outcome for assessing cardioprotective effect, indicating anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC), cardiac damage, and potential for heart failure.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Hypothesized to be improved or show less degradation
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes will be assessed as a primary outcome. Measurements will be taken at baseline (t0), after the end of anthracycline-treatment (t2), and 3 months after t2 (t3).

analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary outcome for assessing cardioprotective effect, serving as an early and sensitive indicator of cardiac dysfunction and anthracycline-related cardiotoxicity (ARC), often preceding a decline in LVEF.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Hypothesized to be preserved or improved (less decline)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Quantitative changes will be assessed as a primary outcome. Measurements will be taken at baseline (t0), after the end of anthracycline-treatment (t2), and 3 months after t2 (t3).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures the percentage of blood pumped out of the left ventricle with each heartbeat, indicating global systolic function and overall cardiac pumping efficiency.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary outcome for assessing cardioprotective effect and cardiac health status; a key indicator of cardiac dysfunction where a decrease of >10% to <53% is often considered cardiotoxicity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes will be assessed as a secondary outcome. Two measurements taken after 5-min and 3-min rest periods, respectively. Additional records if differences > 5 mmHg; average of two stable measurements (difference < 5 mmHg) used for analysis.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates the force exerted by circulating blood on the walls of blood vessels, reflecting cardiovascular load and aiding in the regulation of systemic circulation and tissue perfusion.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Resting state during structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT), measured using a standard automated device.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Secondary outcome for assessing cardiac health, serving as a key indicator of cardiovascular health, hypertension risk, and overall systemic vascular resistance.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes will be assessed as a secondary outcome. Two measurements taken after 5-min and 3-min rest periods, respectively. Additional records if differences > 7 bpm; average of two stable measurements (difference < 7 bpm) used for analysis.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the number of heartbeats per unit of time, indicating cardiac output and influenced by autonomic nervous system activity and cardiovascular fitness.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Resting state during structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT), measured using a standard automated device.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Secondary outcome for assessing cardiac health, serving as an indicator of cardiovascular fitness, autonomic balance, and potential for cardiac stress or disease.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Resting Heart Rate Variability (HRV) indices (SDNN, RMSSD, LF, HF)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes will be assessed as a secondary outcome. First 5 minutes of R-R recording excluded for stabilization; remaining 5 minutes used to calculate SDNN, RMSSD, LF, and HF indices. Artifacts replaced with interpolated adjacent R-R interval values (filter power < low).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the beat-to-beat variation in heart rate, indicating autonomic nervous system balance, cardiac adaptability, and cardiovascular regulation via parasympathetic and sympathetic influences.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Resting state during structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT), measured using a Polar V800 HR monitor with Polar H7 chest strap.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Secondary outcome for assessing cardiac health, serving as an indicator of cardiac autonomic balance, cardiovascular health, and stress response.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Cardiovascular system (derived from Cardiorespiratory Exercise Test (CRET))

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Changes will be assessed as a secondary outcome. Determined as the absolute difference between HR at peak effort during cardiorespiratory exercise test (CRET) and HR at 60 s post-exercise, and 120 s post-exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the rate at which heart rate decreases and returns to resting levels after physical exertion, indicating cardiovascular fitness, autonomic recovery capacity, and autonomic nervous system activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-cardiorespiratory exercise test (CRET) recovery at 60 seconds and 120 seconds during structured exercise program in women with breast cancer undergoing anthracycline-containing chemotherapy (ACT).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Secondary outcome for assessing cardiac health, serving as an indicator of cardiovascular fitness, autonomic function, and potential cardiotoxicity or impaired recovery capacity.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Parameters (Peak V̇o2, Peak RER, Oxygen consumption at Anaerobic Threshold, Total exercise duration, Maximum HR)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Respiratory and cardiovascular systems (measured via expired gases and HR)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Peak V̇o2 (ml/kg/min), Peak RER (ratio of CO2 production to O2 consumption), Oxygen consumption at anaerobic threshold (AT), Total exercise duration (seconds), and Maximum HR achieved during test will be quantified.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Reflects the integrated capacity and functional performance of the cardiovascular, respiratory, and muscular systems to deliver and utilize oxygen during sustained physical activity, indicating aerobic capacity and metabolic efficiency.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Symptom-limited cardiorespiratory exercise test (CRET) on a treadmill using a modified Bruce protocol in a fasted state, within the context of a supervised exercise program.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Primary indicator of aerobic fitness, exercise tolerance, overall cardiovascular health, functional capacity, and resilience to cancer treatment side effects, associated with mortality risk.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Upper Limb Strength (Maximal Voluntary Grip Strength)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Measured in kilograms. Six trials (three per arm, alternating bilateral sequence); results based on the average of the three trials for each arm.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Capacity of skeletal muscles in the upper limbs to generate maximal force.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Maximal voluntary grip strength test using a digital handgrip dynamometer (Saehan Corporation, model SH5003) within the context of the study.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of general muscular strength, sarcopenia, overall health status, and functional capacity.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Score determined by the number of repetitions achieved in 30 seconds.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Functional strength, power, and balance of lower body muscles required for daily activities.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: 30-second sit-to-stand test using a straight-backed chair (40 cm high) within the context of the study.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicator of lower body functional capacity, mobility, fall risk, and independence in daily living.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Self-reported Physical Activity Level (MET minutes/week, sedentary behavior)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: MET minutes per week spent in walking, moderate, and vigorous activities. Sedentary behavior determined as time spent sitting per day (minutes). Participants categorized as low, moderate, or high physical activity level.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Energy expenditure, physical activity habits, and sedentary lifestyle patterns.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-SF), Portuguese language version, within the context of the study.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects general physical activity engagement, sedentary risk, and provides insight into lifestyle factors influencing health.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Health-related Quality of Life (HR-QOL) and Fatigue (EORTC QOL-C30 scales)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Scores from five functional scales (physical, role, cognitive, emotional, social), fatigue scale, and the global health and quality-of-life scale of the EORTC QOL-C30 questionnaire.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Subjective well-being, functional status, and perceived symptom burden in individuals, particularly cancer patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: European Organization for Research and Treatment in Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life C-30 (QOL-C30) questionnaire, third version, Portuguese language, within the context of the study.
